digitalocean-native:kubernetes/v2:Cluste.description: An object specifying custom cluster autoscaler configuration.

expanders.description:
Customizes expanders used by cluster-autoscaler.
The autoscaler will apply each expander from the provided list to narrow down the selection of node types created to scale up,
until either a single node type is left, or the list of expanders is exhausted.
If this flag is unset, autoscaler will use its default expander `random`.
Passing an empty list (_not_ `null`) will unset any previous expander customizations.

Available expanders:
- `random`: Randomly selects a node group to scale.
- `priority`: Selects the node group with the highest priority as per [user-provided configuration](https://docs.digitalocean.com/products/kubernetes/how-to/autoscale/#configuring-priority-expander)
- `least_waste`: Selects the node group that will result in the least amount of idle resources.

scaleDownUnneededTime.description: Used to customize how long a node is unneeded before being scaled down.

scaleDownUtilizationThreshold.description: Used to customize when cluster autoscaler scales down non-empty nodes by setting the node utilization threshold.

Any other value will be accepted but ignored, and `Unknown` will be used in its place.
The slug identifier for the region where the resource will initially be  available.

A status string indicating the state of a custom image. This may be `NEW`,
 `available`, `pending`, `deleted`, or `retired`.

Describes the kind of image. It may be one of `base`, `snapshot`, `backup`, `custom`, or `admin`. Respectively, this specifies whether an image is a DigitalOcean base OS image, user-generated Droplet snapshot, automatically created Droplet backup, user-provided virtual machine image, or an image used for DigitalOcean managed resources (e.g. DOKS worker nodes).

digitalocean-native:tags/v2:Tags.description:
A tag is a label that can be applied to a resource (currently Droplets, Images, Volumes, Volume Snapshots, and Database clusters) in order to better organize or facilitate the lookups and actions on it.
Tags have two attributes: a user defined `name` attribute and an embedded `resources` attribute with information about resources that have been tagged.

name.description:
The name of the tag. Tags may contain letters, numbers, colons, dashes, and underscores.
There is a limit of 255 characters per tag.

**Note:** Tag names are case stable, which means the capitalization you use when you first create a tag is canonical.

When working with tags in the API, you must use the tag's canonical capitalization. For example, if you create a tag named "PROD", the URL to add that tag to a resource would be `https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/tags/PROD/resources` (not `/v2/tags/prod/resources`).

Tagged resources in the control panel will always display the canonical capitalization. For example, if you create a tag named "PROD", you can tag resources in the control panel by entering "prod". The tag will still display with its canonical capitalization, "PROD".

An embedded object containing key value pairs of resource type and resource statistics.
It also includes a count of the total number of resources tagged with the current tag as well as a `last_tagged_uri` attribute set to the last resource tagged with the current tag.

This will only include resources that you are authorized to see. For example, to see tagged Droplets, include the `droplet:read` scope.

Meta.description:
Additional result metadata. Keys include:

- `status`: `requires_approval`, `requires_authorization`, or
  `requires_connection_configuration` when the call stopped before
  running.

- `approval_id`, `tool_name`, `expires_at`, and `decide`: present with
  `requires_approval`. `decide` gives the `method`, `path`, and `body`
  of the approval request to send. Approve the call, then repeat it
  with the same arguments before `expires_at`.

- `retry`: `{"attempt_count": N, "exhausted": bool}` when the gateway
  retried the call.

- `output_view`: the output view applied to the result.
- `cache`: whether the result came from cache, with its age on a hit.

oauthAuthorizationTtlSeconds.description:
How long, in seconds, a user's authorization may be reused before they must consent again. Optional;
0 means 30 days, and the maximum is 100 years.

Authorizations are not refreshed automatically, so this window, not the provider's token lifetime,
decides how often a user is sent back through consent. Set it no longer than the provider's own
token lifetime, so the prompt arrives before a tool call fails against an expired token.

oauthClientId.description: Required for `credentialRefSource` connection: the client ID of your team's OAuth client for the server. Each user of the server then authorizes individually.

oauthClientSecret.description: Required for `credentialRefSource` connection. Write-only; no response returns it.

oauthScopes.description: Required for `credentialRefSource` connection: the scopes to request from each user, 1 to 64 of them.

oauthTokenUrl.description: Required for `credentialRefSource` connection: the OAuth token endpoint, under the same rules as `oauth_authorize_url`.

candidateInferenceConfig.description:
Inference configuration for the candidate model during evaluation.
The output token limit is set automatically and cannot be configured.

candidateModelName.description:
Model slug used to call the candidate model API.
For dedicated inference, this is the model slug from the deployment.
For serverless, this should match the model's internal name.

candidateModelSource.description:
Whether the candidate is a served model (serverless platform, a dedicated
deployment, or a model router) or an OHS-hosted agent config.

candidateModelUuid.description: UUID of the candidate model to evaluate.

datasetUuid.description: UUID of the dataset to use for evaluation.

epochs.description:
How many times each dataset row is evaluated. Defaults to 1, maximum 10.
When more than 1, the results show how consistent the model is across
attempts (avg@k, pass@k, cons@k). Each extra attempt makes the run take
longer. Not saved in presets.

evalRunUuid.description: UUID of the created evaluation run.

judgeModelUuid.description: UUID of the judge model used to score responses.

metricUuids.description: UUIDs of metrics to evaluate (selected from ListModelEvaluationMetrics).

presetSaveSections.description:
Which sections of this run's resolved configuration to persist as a
reusable preset. Each selected section saves only its own fields; the
remaining sections stay empty on the preset and must be supplied inline
on future runs that reference it. Empty means do not save a preset
(unless the deprecated `save_as_preset` boolean is true, in which case
all sections are saved). Ignored when `eval_preset_uuid` is set. Use
`preset_name` to label the saved preset.

queryParams.description: Query params to send with the API requests for this resource.

saveAsPreset.description:
Deprecated: use `preset_save_sections`. When `true` and
`preset_save_sections` is empty, all five sections of the resolved
configuration are saved as a reusable preset (legacy behavior). Ignored
when `eval_preset_uuid` is set.

algorithm.description: This field has been deprecated. You can no longer specify an algorithm for load balancers.

createdAt.description: A time value given in ISO8601 combined date and time format that represents when the load balancer was created.

disableLetsEncryptDnsRecords.description: A boolean value indicating whether to disable automatic DNS record creation for Let's Encrypt certificates that are added to the load balancer.

domains.description: An array of objects specifying the domain configurations for a Global load balancer.

enableBackendKeepalive.description: A boolean value indicating whether HTTP keepalive connections are maintained to target Droplets.

enableProxyProtocol.description: A boolean value indicating whether PROXY Protocol is in use.

firewall.description: An object specifying allow and deny rules to control traffic to the load balancer.

forwardingRules.description: An array of objects specifying the forwarding rules for a load balancer.

glbSettings.description: An object specifying forwarding configurations for a Global load balancer.

healthCheck.description: An object specifying health check settings for the load balancer.

httpIdleTimeoutSeconds.description: An integer value which configures the idle timeout for HTTP requests to the target droplets.

ip.description: An optional IP address to assign to the load balancer from one of your Bring Your Own IP (BYOIP) prefixes. The address must be an unassigned BYOIP address on your account in the same region as the load balancer. If omitted, DigitalOcean assigns a public IP address automatically. This field is only applied when creating the load balancer, cannot be changed afterward, and is not supported for `GLOBAL` or `INTERNAL` load balancers.

ipv6.description: An attribute containing the public-facing IPv6 address of the load balancer.

name.description: A human-readable name for a load balancer instance.

network.description: A string indicating whether the load balancer should be external or internal. Internal load balancers have no public IPs and are only accessible to resources on the same VPC network. This property cannot be updated after creating the load balancer.

networkStack.description: A string indicating whether the load balancer will support IPv4 or both IPv4 and IPv6 networking. This property cannot be updated after creating the load balancer.

projectId.description: The ID of the project that the load balancer is associated with. If no ID is provided at creation, the load balancer associates with the user's default project. If an invalid project ID is provided, the load balancer will not be created.

queryParams.description: Query params to send with the API requests for this resource.

redirectHttpToHttps.description: A boolean value indicating whether HTTP requests to the load balancer on port 80 will be redirected to HTTPS on port 443.

region.description: The slug identifier for the region where the resource will initially be  available.

size.description:
This field has been replaced by the `size_unit` field for all regions except in AMS2, NYC2, and SFO1. Each available load balancer size now equates to the load balancer having a set number of nodes.
* `lb-small` = 1 node
* `lb-medium` = 3 nodes
* `lb-large` = 6 nodes

You can resize load balancers after creation up to once per hour. You cannot resize a load balancer within the first hour of its creation.

sizeUnit.description: How many nodes the load balancer contains. Each additional node increases the load balancer's ability to manage more connections. digitalocean-native:microvms/v2:Microvm.description: The request body for creating a MicroVM. With `source.oci_ref`, `region` and `size` are required. With `source.checkpoint_id`, the MicroVM inherits the checkpoint's region, size, container image, and environment variables, and a different `region` or `size`, or any `environment`, is rejected.

autoPause.description: Automatic pause settings. A MicroVM always pauses after it is idle for `idle_timeout`. Sending `enabled` set to `false` is rejected.

autoResume.description: Whether an HTTP request, command, or console session resumes the MicroVM when it is paused. Set to `false` to require a manual resume.

httpPort.description: The guest port the workload serves HTTP on. Defaults to `8080`. Not returned in responses. When creating from a checkpoint without `ports`, must be one of the checkpoint's ports.

httpProtocol.description: The protocol the HTTP port serves.

microvm.description: A MicroVM. All fields are set at creation. There is no update endpoint.

name.description: The name of the MicroVM. Must be unique in the region and contain 1 to 63 lowercase letters, digits, and hyphens.

networking.description: `public` sends outbound traffic through a shared NAT gateway. `vpc` places the MicroVM in the VPC network set by `vpc_uuid`.

ports.description: The guest ports to declare, up to five. Must include `http_port`. Defaults to only the HTTP port. During the public preview, only the HTTP port is reachable through the MicroVM's endpoint.

queryParams.description: Query params to send with the API requests for this resource.

region.description: The slug of the region to create the MicroVM in. Required with `source.oci_ref`.

size.description: The MicroVM's size. `cpu` and `memory` must be one of the pairs `1`/`2048`, `2`/`4096`, `8`/`16384`, or `16`/`32768`. The size sets the disk, which is returned in responses.

source.description: What the MicroVM runs. Set exactly one of `oci_ref` or `checkpoint_id`.

tags.description: Tags to apply to the MicroVM.

vpcUuid.description: The ID of a VPC network in the same region that belongs to your team. Required when `networking` is `vpc`.

autoPause.description: Automatic pause settings. A MicroVM always pauses after it is idle for `idle_timeout`. Sending `enabled` set to `false` is rejected.

autoResume.description: Whether an HTTP request, command, or console session resumes the MicroVM when it is paused. Set to `false` to require a manual resume.

httpPort.description: The guest port the workload serves HTTP on. Defaults to `8080`. Not returned in responses. When creating from a checkpoint without `ports`, must be one of the checkpoint's ports.

httpProtocol.description: The protocol the HTTP port serves.

digitalocean-native:tags/v2:Tag.description:
A tag is a label that can be applied to a resource (currently Droplets, Images, Volumes, Volume Snapshots, and Database clusters) in order to better organize or facilitate the lookups and actions on it.
Tags have two attributes: a user defined `name` attribute and an embedded `resources` attribute with information about resources that have been tagged.

name.description:
The name of the tag. Tags may contain letters, numbers, colons, dashes, and underscores.
There is a limit of 255 characters per tag.

**Note:** Tag names are case stable, which means the capitalization you use when you first create a tag is canonical.

When working with tags in the API, you must use the tag's canonical capitalization. For example, if you create a tag named "PROD", the URL to add that tag to a resource would be `https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/tags/PROD/resources` (not `/v2/tags/prod/resources`).

Tagged resources in the control panel will always display the canonical capitalization. For example, if you create a tag named "PROD", you can tag resources in the control panel by entering "prod". The tag will still display with its canonical capitalization, "PROD".

queryParams.description: Query params to send with the API requests for this resource.

resources.description:
An embedded object containing key value pairs of resource type and resource statistics.
It also includes a count of the total number of resources tagged with the current tag as well as a `last_tagged_uri` attribute set to the last resource tagged with the current tag.

This will only include resources that you are authorized to see. For example, to see tagged Droplets, include the `droplet:read` scope.

Meta.description:
Additional result metadata. Keys include:

- `status`: `requires_approval`, `requires_authorization`, or
  `requires_connection_configuration` when the call stopped before
  running.

- `approval_id`, `tool_name`, `expires_at`, and `decide`: present with
  `requires_approval`. `decide` gives the `method`, `path`, and `body`
  of the approval request to send. Approve the call, then repeat it
  with the same arguments before `expires_at`.

- `retry`: `{"attempt_count": N, "exhausted": bool}` when the gateway
  retried the call.

- `output_view`: the output view applied to the result.
- `cache`: whether the result came from cache, with its age on a hit.
